subject: Order worksheet: reserve-ceiling safeguards & packaging mapping
messages:
From: Tracy Monroe <procurement@aegiscloud.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 May 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on order worksheet: 'Reserve Ceiling' and packaging mapping

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We reviewed the order worksheet you shared and have a few open items on the pricing exhibit before procurement can push to legal:

- Reserve ceiling: The current paragraph allows Redwood to designate a 'reserve' number of units and charge at full rate up to the reserve. We need clarity on whether that reserve is a hard billing commitment or a soft buffer that becomes refundable if usage stays below X for a period.
- Floor / true-up mechanics: The exhibit references a quarterly true-up but doesn't define how unused reserve is reconciled (credit vs. future offset).
- Packaging mapping: Our SKU model bundles inference credits across chat and embeddings; the worksheet maps to token units but we need an invoice sample showing mapping at the line-item level.

Attached: aegis_orderworkbook.xlsx (worksheet with our expected monthly mapping).

We'd prefer: a soft-reserve model with a 60% utilization threshold over a rolling 90-day window that triggers a partial refund/credit, rather than a permanent hard commitment. If Redwood insists on a hard reserve for capacity planning, can we get a step-down schedule if committed utilization is not met for two consecutive quarters?

Can you have legal/ops review and share suggested redlines? Happy to hop on a 30-min call early next week.

Best,
Tracy Monroe
Sr. Procurement Manager | AegisCloud
procurement@aegiscloud.com

Attachments: aegis_orderworkbook.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48 KB)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Tracy Monroe <procurement@aegiscloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 May 2025 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on order worksheet: 'Reserve Ceiling' and packaging mapping

Tracy —

Thanks for walking through the worksheet and for the clear asks. Quick responses below and I've attached a proposed amendment for discussion.

High-level reply:
- Reserve ceiling: We can support a hybrid approach. Redwood prefers a committed reserve for capacity planning (so we can lock GPU pools), but we'll accept a 2-step step-down schedule if actual utilization is below the agreed threshold for two consecutive quarters. See Section 2 of the attached proposed amendment for language.
- True-up mechanics: We propose quarterly true-ups where unused credits are converted to a one-time credit against the next invoice in month 1 of the following quarter. If usage remains below 50% after two consecutive quarters, the reserve steps down 25%.
- Packaging mapping: Attached is a sample invoice mapping and a short appendix that maps your SKU bundles to our token/embedding units.

Next steps: I've attached redwood_proposed_amendment_v1.docx with marked clauses for the reserve, step-down schedule, and invoice mapping. Can we schedule a 30-min slot Thursday or Friday? If legal needs different wording, loop them in and we can iterate quickly.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Attachments: redwood_proposed_amendment_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 32 KB)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 May 2025 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Legal markup suggestions for AGG-2025-1247 (reserve/step-down)

Markus / Karthik —

Internal notes from Legal/Revenue Ops after quick triage of the proposed amendment:

- "Reserve" vs "Commitment": prefer term 'Committed Reserve' with a defined reconciliation path. Avoid language that creates a refundable liability; instead, use credit mechanics tied to invoice offsets to keep accounting treatment straightforward.
- Step-down schedule: replace the proposed flat 25% step-down with a matrix tied to utilization bands (e.g., <50% -> 40% step-down; 50–70% -> 25%; >70% -> no change). This gives us more predictable revenue recognition.
- Billing sample: require a one-line example in Exhibit B showing: (1) committed units; (2) actual usage; (3) quarterly credit calculation; (4) invoice line showing the credit. This reduces back-and-forth with their billing team.
- Attachment: legal_markup_redlines.pdf with inline suggested language and an alternative 'soft-reserve' carveout if procurement insists.

Recommendation: propose the matrix above and keep the automatic invoice credit approach. If Aegis insists on refunds instead of credits, escalate to Finance for approval.

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: legal_markup_redlines.pdf (application/pdf, 14 KB)

From: Kevin Ortiz <kevin.ortiz@aegiscloud.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Tracy Monroe <procurement@aegiscloud.com>
Date: Thu, 8 May 2025 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on order worksheet: 'Reserve Ceiling' and packaging mapping

On Thu, May 8, 2025 at 09:17 AM laura_bennett@redwood.com wrote:
> Internal notes from Legal/Revenue Ops after quick triage of the proposed amendment:
> - "Reserve" vs "Commitment": prefer term 'Committed Reserve' with a defined reconciliation path.

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Markus / Laura. Aegis is fine with credits instead of cash refunds, provided the credit calculation is explicit and the credit can be applied to any Redwood invoice within 12 months. Two clarifications:

1) Utilization bands: your proposed matrix looks reasonable. Please include a worked example: if we commit to 1,000 units / month, but actual average is 520 units, how does the step-down trigger and what credit posts on the next invoice?
2) Packaging mapping: we really need a CSV example with line items. I've attached our internal sample so your billing team can map directly.

Attached: aegis_pricing_samples.csv

If you can incorporate the matrix and a one-page worked example into the amendment, we can expedite our procurement review. If possible, include a DocuSign-ready orderform so our legal team can route it.

Kevin Ortiz
Head of Cloud Procurement | AegisCloud
kevin.ortiz@aegiscloud.com

Attachments: aegis_pricing_samples.csv (text/csv, 5 KB)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Tracy Monroe <procurement@aegiscloud.com>, Kevin Ortiz <kevin.ortiz@aegiscloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 May 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Final redlines and worked example (requested) — AGG-2025-1247

Team —

Appreciate the constructive back-and-forth. Attached is a consolidated redline (orderform_exhibitB_final_redline.docx) and a one-page worked example inserted into Exhibit B. Summary of the agreed points:

- Commitment model retained: 'Committed Reserve' remains in Exhibit B for capacity guarantees.
- Step-down matrix added: utilization bands with percentage step-downs and formula for quarterly calculation.
- Credit mechanics: unused committed units convert to an invoice credit applied against any Redwood invoice within 12 months. Credits are non-refundable.
- Worked example: shows 1,000 committed units, 520 average usage -> triggers the 50% band logic and results in a step-down + calculated credit applied on next invoice. See Exhibit B, Section 3.
- Invoice mapping: Exhibit B now includes a sample CSV line-item mapping so your billing team can reconcile tokens to bundle SKUs.

DocuSign: I've initiated a DocuSign envelope with the updated orderform for signature: https://www.docusign.com/00A12345 (placeholder). If Aegis is happy with the wording, please sign and we'll schedule the rollout and capacity provisioning.

If you want one last 20-min call to walk legal through the worked example, I'm available Monday AM.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182
